column1: # mapping_set_title: Digital twin: Asset Administration Shell 3.2 and AutomationML 2.1

column9: comment

An AAS is serialised as an internal element with the role class AssetAdministrationShellRoleClassLib/AssetAdministrationShell, named by its idShort (AR 004E rules 2, 14 and 16). Its id becomes the value of an AutomationML attribute, not the internal element's ID, which stays a UUID.
A property aas:AssetAdministrationShell and aml:InternalElement share.

The asset an AAS describes is an internal element with the role class AssetAdministrationShellRoleClassLib/Asset (AR 004E 5.1.2). The recommendation was written for AAS metamodel 2.0, where the asset was an identifiable of its own; in 3.x it is the shell's asset information, with no idShort to name the element by.

A submodel of kind Instance is an internal element with the role class AssetAdministrationShellRoleClassLib/Submodel, named by its idShort, inside the shell's internal element (AR 004E rules 2, 16 and 5.1.3).
A property aas:Submodel and aml:InternalElement share.

A submodel of kind Template, and the shell holding it, become system unit classes in a system unit class library, e.g. AssetAdministrationShellSystemUnitClasses, carrying the same roles as their instances (AR 004E rules 24 to 26).

Every submodel element is an internal element whose role class is its subtype, e.g. AssetAdministrationShellRoleClassLib/Property, named by its idShort; a collection's elements are internal elements inside it (AR 004E rules 9 and 13).
A property aas:SubmodelElement and aml:InternalElement share.

A File element's internal element references its file through a FileDataReference interface, derived from ExternalDataReference, whose refURI and MIMEType attributes carry the file's path and content type (AR 004E rule 10 and 4.7).

A reference element pointing inside the AAS has a ReferableReference interface, joined by an internal link to the element it refers to; an external reference is a serialised string instead (AR 004E rule 11).
A relationship element's first and second elements are ReferableReference interfaces, each joined by an internal link to the element it refers to when that is inside the AAS (AR 004E rule 11).

A concept description is an internal element with the role class AssetAdministrationShellRoleClassLib/ConceptDescription, in an instance hierarchy such as AssetAdministrationShellConceptDescriptions. Its name joins its idShort, ID type and ID, so the names don't match (AR 004E rules 15 and 20).
A qualifier is a complex attribute named Qualifier:<type>=<value>, with the qualifier's own attributes as nested attributes (AR 004E rule 7).

A reference-valued attribute of an AAS element, e.g. its semanticId, is an attribute whose value is the reference serialised as a string (AR 004E rule 6 and 6.2.6). The attribute's RefSemantic, e.g. AAS:HasSemantics/semanticId, names the metamodel attribute it holds, not the reference's meaning.

An AAS property can publish an AutomationML attribute of the element that holds the asset's engineering data, named as the attribute and holding its value; the recommendation relates them by a RelationshipElement in the AutomationML submodel, or by a property already in another submodel such as the Digital Nameplate (AR AMLinAAS 3.3).
A property aas:Property and aml:Attribute share.
A property aas:Property and aml:Attribute share.

An attribute published as a property shares its meaning: the key of the property's semanticId, e.g. an ECLASS IRDI, is the path the attribute's RefSemantic gives. AR 004E uses RefSemantic differently, for the AAS metamodel attribute an attribute serialises (6.2.5), so this holds for published engineering attributes, not for a serialised AAS.
A property aas:Key and aml:RefSemantic share.
